t: An empire of the Jurchen people of Manchuria, founded by Wanyan Aguda in 1115 and named Jin, 'gold'.
It destroyed the Liao, took the Song capital Kaifeng in 1127 and ruled northern China, moving its capital to Beijing in 1153.
Mongol invasions from 1211 drove the court to Kaifeng, and the dynasty ended at Caizhou in 1234.
dyk: In 1127 Jin armies carried off two Song emperors, Huizong and his son Qinzong, to Manchuria, where both died in captivity.
ev: Wanyan Aguda proclaims the Great Jin
Jin capture the Liao emperor Tianzuo, ending the Liao state
Jin take Kaifeng and carry off two Song emperors
The Treaty of Shaoxing fixes the Song border on the Huai River
Prince Hailing moves the capital to Zhongdu (Beijing)
Genghis Khan invades and defeats the Jin at Yehuling
Caizhou falls and Emperor Aizong takes his own life

f.predecessor: Liao dynasty; Northern Song (in northern China)
